correctness.rationale: A compactly cutoff local oscillation u_j=(eta_j/k_j) chi sin(k_j x1) has C0 size O(eta/k), C1 size O(eta) and Hessian magnitude >=c eta k. Multiplying radius R(1+u_j) by c_j=[average(1+u_j)^(n+1)]^(-1/(n+1)) enforces the enclosed volume exactly; c_j=1+O(eta/k) preserves annular closeness and normal-angle control via (1+|grad rho|²/rho²)^(-1/2). The radial second fundamental form contains Hessian term and bounded lower-order terms, so choose k to exceed arbitrary L_j. Two points separated ~1/k exhibit normal difference >=c eta, and choosing k_j so eta_j k_j^(1/m)>=j for all m<=j forces each fixed alpha>0 seminorm to diverge. This is a valid analytic construction for every fixed n>=1, not an evolution blow-up.

value.rationale: FAIL: The exact-volume rescaling is a one-scalar normalization and the prescribed curvature/Hölder divergences are immediate from the textbook oscillation (eta/k)sin(kx). The main source expressly works with first-order assumptions without requiring curvature or a normal modulus. The construction offers no nontrivial sharp threshold, obstruction to the cited flow theorem, independent geometric invariant, classification or difficult boundary; it restates routine C1 not controlling C2 in spherical coordinates. It is illustrative but not a substantive mathematical gap under the required value criterion.

final_claim: For arbitrary sequences epsilon_j,theta_j->0 and L_j->infinity, exactly volume-normalized smooth radial spheres can satisfy annular and normal-angle closeness while sup curvature >= L_j and all positive Hölder normal seminorms diverge.
limitations: This is only a static noncompactness witness; it neither contradicts nor informs existence/regularization of the flow beyond illustrating why curvature is not assumed.
